summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload on npm install
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is variable-name-obfuscated and, when no local `bun` is found, downloads a Bun runtime zip from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases (v1.3.13), extracts the platform-specific `bun` binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it on the sibling file `math_init.js`. No hash or signature verification is performed on the downloaded runtime. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB heavily obfuscated `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle using a shuffled string-array decoder (`n7gIxM` / `WV8StW` / `hc1jfK9`); its contents have no correspondence to the package's advertised React chatbot UI code in `dist/` or `src/`. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: a second language runtime is fetched at install time specifically so that opaque, obfuscated install-time code executes outside the Node-based tooling that ordinarily inspects package installs. The chain fires automatically on `npm install` via the `preinstall` lifecycle hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
